key_insight: RGR builds recursive gradient estimates in Euclidean space before mapping them to Stiefel tangent spaces, avoiding vector transport while retaining convergence guarantees.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports orthogonality-constrained learning with fewer tuning requirements, including applications to PCA, matrix completion, and orthogonal neural networks.
method: Estimate gradients recursively in Euclidean space, map to tangent space, and update via retraction.
Finite-sum RGR-SPIDER uses an adaptive stepsize requiring neither the gradient Lipschitz constant nor a fixed iteration horizon.
Online RGR-SRM and RGR-EMA require neither prescribed large mini-batches nor a fixed iteration horizon.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports faster empirical convergence on PCA, low-rank matrix completion, and orthogonal convolutional networks, plus an RGR-SPIDER bound of O(N + √N ε⁻²) component-gradient evaluations to reach ε-criticality.
watch_item: Faster empirical convergence does not necessarily imply lower wall-clock cost; tangent mapping and retraction overhead should be benchmarked.
paper_title: Recursive Gradient Retraction Methods for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization on Stiefel Manifolds
